items.title: CSOs reject five-year presidential term, demand changes to MMDCE election proposal
items.description: Civil society organisations (CSOs) have rejected the proposed extension of Ghana’s presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years, while demanding changes to government proposals on the election of Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs). The groups argue that the existing four-year mandate, which allows a President to seek re-election for a second term, is sufficient for elected officials to implement their governance programmes. They also insist that citizens must be allowed to elect their local government leaders without presidential interference. The positions emerged from a two-day engagement between the Constitutional Reform Implementation Committee (CREC) and more than 100 civil society organisations as part of efforts to build consensus on proposed amendments to Ghana’s 1992 Constitution. The Executive Secretary of the Committee, Oliver Barker-Vormawor, said the engagement had made significant progress, with civil society organisations agreeing with approximately 89 per cent of the government’s proposed reforms. “Over the past two days we’ve been engaging with over a hundred civil society organizations to build consensus around some of the packet of reforms. We’re at a stage where civil society is coming out with resolutions on some of the things that they agree with,” he said. “So many of the other issues, I think that about 89% of what the government is proposing, civil society organizations are agreed with that, and so we have made significant headway.” Mr Barker-Vormawor said the discussions had also helped reduce the number of outstanding issues from an initial 41 to 10. He explained that the Committee had been engaging stakeholders to identify areas of agreement and disagreement, with unresolved matters to be referred to Cabinet for possible reconsideration. “Now the issues on which we are not able to reach some consensus, in particular the question of the four or five-year term, for instance the demand for MPs not to be ministers, those questions we have a mandate to refer back to Cabinet, because the decision-maker is Cabinet, for Cabinet then to revisit its positions on those issues,” he said. He stressed that the Committee’s responsibility was to accurately communicate the concerns raised by stakeholders rather than independently alter the government’s position. “Our understanding is that the document is a Cabinet position, which then means that for changes to happen, Cabinet has to reconsider,” he added. The proposed extension of the presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years remains one of the major contentious issues in the reform discussions. Koku Anyidoho, an adviser to the General Secretary of the Christian Council of Ghana, said the participating groups were united in opposing the proposal. He said 18 position papers had been presented during the two-day engagement, with stakeholders reaching broad agreement on several issues. “Two specific issues that come up is the fact that, to a man, that is every grouping here gathered, does not accept the government position on increasing the term limits of the President from four years to five years. Same as the MPs,” he said. Mr Anyidoho argued that the existing arrangement, which allows a President to seek a second four-year term, provides sufficient time to implement a governance agenda. “They believe that within the four-year space, it should be possible to carry out a governance agenda that will sit well. The person gets four years, gets another four years, that’s eight years. It looks like the consensus is that that is enough,” he stated. The Head of Programmes at Star Ghana Foundation and co-convener of the Citizens Platform on Constitutional Reforms, Eunice Rachel Agbenyadzi, also said maintaining the four-year presidential term was among the positions supported by stakeholders. She explained that the Constitution Review Commission had proposed a five-year presidential term, which the government endorsed but other political parties rejected. “One of the things is maintain the presidential term at four years,” she said. MMDCE elections The proposed election of MMDCEs also featured prominently in the discussions, with stakeholders supporting direct elections but raising concerns about the government’s proposed arrangements. Mr Anyidoho explained that although the government’s position paper agrees with the Constitution Review Commission’s recommendation for the election of MMDCEs, it proposes a process that would allow the President to nominate candidates. He said the proposal initially provided for five presidential nominees, a number that was subsequently reduced to three, from whom one person would be elected. However, civil society organisations want the President completely removed from the process. “The government position paper was like, okay, there will be election, but whoever is President will nominate five persons. It’s watered down to three, and then one is voted for,” he explained. “Of course, a cross-board consensus has been built that no, the presidency or the President of central government should have no hand in that election process, and that for our decentralization and local governance process to really have greater roots, let’s allow the base to elect their own MMDCEs,” he added. Ms Agbenyadzi said the groups believe direct elections would make local government leaders more accountable to the people they serve. She, however, noted that discussions were still ongoing over whether the elections should be conducted on a partisan or non-partisan basis. “There is consensus that there should be election. Now what we need to figure out is whether it should be on a partisan basis, which some of the parties hold views on,” she said. She also said civil society organisations had rejected the government’s proposal to introduce a nomination process for the elections, insisting that there should be no restrictions or filters on who can contest. MPs as ministers Another major issue is whether Members of Parliament should continue to be appointed as ministers. Ms Agbenyadzi said citizens were concerned that allowing MPs to serve in ministerial positions could weaken Parliament’s ability to effectively perform its oversight responsibilities. She said the government’s position was to retain discretion over the number of MPs the President could appoint as ministers, but civil society organisations were advocating a stricter separation of powers. “This is a very sensitive issue. Citizens are saying no, because we believe that a strong Parliament delivers good governance for Ghana,” she said. “The point is that the government says, give us discretion. Don’t restrict that in terms of how many MPs can be appointed as ministers, but the consensus here is that there should be strict separation of powers,” she added. Mr Barker-Vormawor confirmed that the appointment of MPs as ministers was among the issues on which stakeholders had not reached consensus and which the Committee intended to refer to Cabinet. Proportional representation The introduction of proportional representation in Ghana’s electoral system is another issue under consideration. Ms Agbenyadzi said the proposal was intended to address the inadequate representation of groups such as women, young people and persons with disabilities in governance. She explained that the Constitution Review Commission recommended that the country consider introducing the system following a study to determine how it could be implemented. However, the government has proposed beginning with a pilot involving 24 parliamentary seats. “The evidence shows clearly that there are certain groups like women, young people, persons with disabilities that are not well represented in governance,” she said. She added that stakeholders believed the proposal should be approached carefully, with further assessment of how the system would work. Mr Barker-Vormawor also pointed to other proposals under consideration, including ending the payment of ex gratia, introducing a binding national development plan, requiring the President to pay tax and directly electing district chief executives. He said the ultimate decision on proposals requiring a referendum would rest with the Ghanaian electorate. “A hundred civil society organisations and a constitutional committee can agree, but the people of Ghana will go and say no. Our job is that they understand what they are going to vote for and then they express their view,” he said. CSOs call for broader consultations The renewed engagement has also been welcomed by civil society organisations, which say the process must remain open to different stakeholder perspectives. Ms Agbenyadzi said the Citizens Platform on Constitutional Reforms, convened by Star Ghana Foundation, the Centre for Democratic Development (CDD) and Democracy Hub, had spent the past two years building public understanding and momentum around the reform process. She said one of the concerns raised by the platform following the government’s position paper and the inauguration of CREC was the need to clarify the Committee’s mandate, particularly its responsibility to build consensus beyond the government’s proposals. According to her, the Committee had since become more receptive to position papers and recommendations from other groups. “We really, really think that this is progressive because we believe that it offers us the opportunity to build this constitutional reform process as a national project where different stakeholders’ inputs are recognized and are honored, even when we cannot agree on everything,” she said. She said stakeholders had agreed that the Committee should continue engaging civil society organisations through further dialogue, meetings and the submission of memoranda. She also called for dedicated engagement with the New Patriotic Party (NPP), describing it as a critical stakeholder whose views must be considered to ensure that all political interests were represented in the process. Mr Anyidoho said the renewed consultations were important, particularly after concerns that the consultative process had ended. He welcomed the Committee’s decision to reopen discussions and create opportunities for more groups to participate. “Without building consensus and engaging in a process that has a lot of integrity, then it creates a lot of challenges,” he said. Public education crucial to referendum Beyond reaching agreement on the proposed amendments, stakeholders say public education will be crucial, particularly for changes to entrenched provisions of the Constitution. Mr Anyidoho warned that inadequate civic education could undermine the entire reform process, as the Constitution requires significant voter participation and support for entrenched amendments to be approved. He explained that at least 40 per cent of registered voters must participate in the referendum, with 75 per cent of those voting required to support the proposed amendments. “Until you get good civic education, good public engagement, you’re not going to get the buying, and the numbers are there on the voters register. Once we finish voting, we don’t have the numbers. Then it derails the whole process,” he said. He called for coordinated public education to help citizens understand the proposed changes and appreciate their importance before the referendum. Mr Barker-Vormawor also emphasised that the people of Ghana would ultimately determine whether the proposals requiring a referendum should be adopted. He noted that while non-entrenched amendments would go through Parliament, the House would have to undertake its own deliberations and secure the required two-thirds majority. “We are not looking for Parliament to settle all disagreements before the bill is laid. Parliament is a deliberative body, they are going to deliberate on them, convince people to vote or not vote,” he said. He added that previous constitutional amendment bills had failed to secure the required parliamentary support, underscoring the need for consensus-building within the House. The engagement ended with stakeholders expressing support for continued consultations and public education as the Committee prepares to present outstanding issues to Cabinet. With 10 issues still requiring further consideration, the next stage of the process will depend on the government’s response to the concerns raised and whether the emerging consensus can be sustained through the parliamentary and referendum stages.

items.title: Frente Amplio evoca el espíritu de 2023 para “volver a ganar” las generales

items.title: Relance de la Mine de Perkoa : C’est une mine 100℅burkinabè, une première en Afrique selon le Président du Faso
items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a présidé la cérémonie de relance des activités de la mine polymétallique de Perkouan dans la commune de Réo, province du Sanguié, région du Nando. Les activités de la mine de Perkoaun ont repris. Les machines vrombissent et les travailleurs sont à l’ouvrage, en présence du Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, qui a procédé à la visite des installations après le dévoilement de la plaque inaugurale et la coupure du ruban. À travers la relance de cette activité, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ réaffirme sa vision souverainiste. « On ne peut continuer à laisser brader nos ressources, que tout sorte et qu’on nous serve des miettes. Aujourd’hui nous reprenons le contrôle de notre sous-sol », a-t-il souligné. « Notre énergie c’est la souveraineté. Quand vous voyez l’histoire de cette mine, après quatre années de pause, elle a été entièrement réhabilitée par des ingénieurs burkinabè. Cela veut dire que nous avons la connaissance, nous avons la capacité. Cette mine appartient à 100% à l’État », a expliqué le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. « Le Burkina est l’un des rares pays, sinon le seul pays en Afrique à avoir autant de mines industrielles qui lui appartiennent à 100%. Lorsqu’on pense à cette souveraineté, ça ne peut qu’être votre carburant pour évoluer dans cette lutte », a précisé le Président du Faso. La présence du Chef de l’État en personne pour la remise en fonction de cette unité d’exploitation minière témoigne de son engagement personnel pour l’exploitation endogène de nos ressources naturelles. Elle marque également un tournant très important pour le secteur minier dans la région. items.title: RON Foundation invests in digital education at Atwima Koforidua with modern ICT lab commissioning
items.description: A philanthropic organization, RON Foundation, has cut the sod for the construction of a modern Information and Communication Technology (ICT) laboratory at Atwima Koforidua in the Ashanti Region to boost digital and Artificial Intelligence (AI) education among pupils in the area. The project, with an estimated cost of GH¢750,000, is anticipated to be completed within a period of nine to twelve months, and is expected to be equipped with 32 computers as well as a printer, scanner and photocopier. The laboratory, which will accommodate computers for 30 pupils and two others for supervisors, will have networking infrastructure and appropriate furniture, among other essential learning accessories. Speaking at the sod-cutting ceremony, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the Foundation, Ing. Richard Okyere Nketia, said the initiative forms part of his commitment to bridging the digital divide and promoting quality education in the Atwima Nwabiagya North District. He stressed that early exposure to digital learning is key, noting that children who are introduced to technology at a young age are better positioned to compete in a global economy that is increasingly driven by innovation, data and digital tools. According to him, the centre would equip pupils of his alma mater with AI knowledge, technology and IT skills, which he described as critical to development in the modern world. “My decision to fund the ICT centre was born out of my personal connection to the town and concern about the poor state of infrastructure at my former school, Atwima Koforidua D/A Basic School,” he said. The Ghanaian civil and structural engineer is positive that the facility, when completed, would not only transform teaching and learning at the school but also open opportunities for the wider Atwima Koforidua community to acquire digital skills. “Our vision is to create a facility where technology becomes an everyday learning tool rather than a privilege available only to children in well-resourced schools. We are not just building an ICT centre; we are building access, opportunity, and a brighter future for our children,” he stated. Beyond the Koforidua project, the RON Foundation CEO encouraged collective participation in national development. Ing. Nketia said nation-building should not be left to government alone, stressing that individuals who have benefited from the country have a duty to give back to society. He urged people who have risen through education and opportunity in Ghana to remember the communities that shaped them and to return to support the next generation. “If everyone does a little in their own hometown, the whole country will move forward,” he said. “I will therefore appeal to Ghanaians in the diaspora, old students, philanthropists, churches, corporate bodies and other well-meaning individuals to invest in their hometowns’ development.” The School Improvement Support Officer (SISO) for the Akropong Circuit of the Atwima Nwabiagya North Education Directorate, Mr. Steven Anim Adu, described the ultra-modern ICT laboratory project as a major boost to teaching and learning. He explained that many pupils in various basic schools in the district do not have direct access to computers and therefore learn ICT largely in theory, which limits their practical understanding of the subject. “Direct access to computers will give our schoolchildren the practical aspect of computing. When they have constant contact with computers, it will help them learn better and improve education in the school,” he said. Mr. Anim Adu commended Ing. Richard Okyere Nketia and his foundation for the project. This intervention comes at a time when Ghana is pushing to deepen digital literacy from the basic school level, with ICT now a core subject at the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) level and a growing national conversation about AI, coding and STEM education. For many rural and peri-urban basic schools, however, access remains a major challenge. Pupils often learn ICT largely in theory, without computers to practise on, a situation that affects their confidence, performance and interest in technology-related careers. The new centre at Atwima Koforidua is therefore expected to bridge that gap, giving pupils the opportunity to learn through hands-on practice, rather than theoretical learning.

items.title: Galamsey, erratic weather cause unprecedented decline in Ghana’s cocoa production – Kuapa Kokoo MD
items.description: Concerns over the future of Ghana’s cocoa industry are growing, as farmers warn that the destruction of forest reserves, illegal mining and changing climate patterns could further undermine cocoa production. The activities of illegal miners, popularly known as galamsey and chainsaw operators are not only destroying forest cover but also polluting water bodies and threatening the survival of cocoa farms in several farming communities across the country. The concerns dominated discussions at the 32nd Annual Delegates Conference of Kuapa Kokoo Farmers, held under the theme “ Protecting Our Forest, Securing Our Future. “ Addressing the conference, the Managing Director of Kuapa Kokoo, Emmanuel Kwabena Arthur, raised serious concerns about the low cocoa production recorded this year, describing the current situation as unprecedented. “First of all, we have a problem with production itself. For the first time, as far as I am concerned, at the peak of the season, we don’t have a lot of cocoa available, and that is unprecedented,” he said. He noted that with the season approaching the end of November, cocoa production should be very high, but the situation on the ground tells a different story. “Around this time, as we get to the end of November, cocoa production should be very high, but when you go to the bush and you see the trees, the kind of pods you see on the trees is not encouraging,” he added. Mr. Arthur said many cocoa farms have been abandoned and taken over by galamsey operators, reducing the total hectares of land available for cocoa production. According to him, illegal mining activities have also polluted river bodies, leaving farmers without clean water to irrigate their farms and to mix pesticides and insecticides to treat their cocoa. “Farmers don’t get clean water to water their farms and to also get clean water for their pesticides and insecticides to actually treat the cocoa. All these things are affecting cocoa production,” he said. Touching on other factors contributing to the low cocoa production, he pointed to changing climate patterns. According to him, it had disrupted rainfall distribution and affected flowering and pod formation on cocoa trees. He explained that the erratic weather conditions is making it difficult for farmers to predict planting and farm maintenance schedules, further worsening the already declining output from cocoa farms across the country. Mr. Arthur warned that production for the season could fall further below expectations, contrary to earlier projections by the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD). “COCOBOD has even projected that there will be less produce this year than we got last year, but I believe that if we are not careful, the production level will be very low, lower than what we actually expect,” he said. The Kuapa Kokoo Managing Director is urging government to strengthen the fight against illegal mining and chainsaw operations, particularly in forest reserves and cocoa-growing communities, to protect the country’s cocoa industry and secure the future of farmers. Meanwhile, the National President of the Kuapa Kokoo Farmers Cocoa Cooperative and Marketing Union, James Agyekum Kwarteng, has expressed deep concern over the declining interest of the youth in agriculture, particularly in the cocoa sector. According to him, the situation is becoming alarming as most of the cocoa farmers currently engaged in production are aged. He revealed that such a development poses a serious threat to the future sustainability of cocoa production in the country if nothing is done to address it. He also called on the government to introduce deliberate policies and interventions to support young people in the agricultural sector. Mr. Agyekum Kwarteng is of the view that such measures would help motivate other youngsters to venture into farming and ensure the continuity of cocoa production for generations to come. The conference brought together delegates, farmers, management and stakeholders from across the Union’s operational areas to review its performance, discuss challenges facing cocoa farmers and chart a way forward for sustainable cocoa production.

items.title: Mock ballot papers won’t feature party names, logos – INEC
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained that sample ballot papers for its nationwide mock accreditation exercise will not carry political party names or logos because the exercise is designed to test election technology rather than promote any political party. INEC Deputy Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Wilfred Ifogah, gave the explanation during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, ahead of the exercise scheduled for Saturday, November 28. Ifogah said the mock accreditation was a non-partisan exercise intended to assess the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections. He explained that the exercise would allow INEC to test its equipment and give voters an idea of what the accreditation and voting processes would look like during the elections. “This is a mock exercise; we are not using it for any partisanship event. It is just something for those who come out to feel a sense of participation”, he said. According to him, election materials have already been deployed to the selected polling units across the country. The exercise will take place in 17,676 polling units, covering two polling units in each of Nigeria’s 8,838 registration areas. INEC is expected to deploy the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and its electronic results upload technology to assess their reliability ahead of the general elections. The mock accreditation will run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., with the commission hoping that the exercise will strengthen public confidence in the electoral process. The 2027 general elections are scheduled to begin with the presidential and National Assembly polls on January 16, while the governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections will hold on February 6. The commission’s mock exercise forms part of its preparations for the polls, allowing it to test its technology and electoral procedures before election day. items.title: Programme avec le FMI : Nérée Noumon juge la dette guinéenne « parmi les meilleures » et assure qu’aucune mesure n’a été imposée
items.description: Le représentant résident du Fonds monétaire international (FMI) en Guinée, Nérée Noumon, a tenu à rassurer sur les conditions d’endettement du pays dans le cadre du nouvel accord conclu avec l’institution financière internationale. Selon lui, la dette contractée bénéficie de conditions financières particulièrement avantageuses. Il a également assuré qu’aucune mesure n’avait été imposée aux autorités guinéennes dans le cadre de ce programme de 425 millions de dollars. Présent ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 à la conférence de presse animée conjointement par la ministre de l’Économie, des Finances et du Budget et le gouverneur de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée, le représentant résident du FMI est revenu sur les principales dispositions de cet accord, notamment la question des subventions et les engagements pris par les autorités guinéennes. Abordant la question des subventions, Nérée Noumon a précisé que les échanges avec le conseil d’administration du FMI portaient essentiellement sur l’élaboration d’une stratégie visant à réduire progressivement leur poids, tout en préservant les populations les plus vulnérables. « Il n’y a rien qui a été imposé aux autorités guinéennes. Mais en ce qui concerne la question spécifique des subventions, dans le communiqué de presse qui a été publié sur la position du conseil d’administration, il ne s’agissait pas de réduire les subventions, mais d’avoir une stratégie de réduction. Déjà, les autorités le feront quand elles seront prêtes et il y a un certain nombre d’actions qui doivent passer en amont : des consultations, de la communication, des mesures d’accompagnement. Ça peut prendre du temps. Il faut faire en sorte qu’il y ait les éléments nécessaires, que ce soit au niveau des moyens de transport et d’autres choses, et identifier les personnes vulnérables. Ça, c’est très important. C’est dans ce cadre que, dans le cadre du programme, les autorités sont engagées à continuer à renforcer les mécanismes de ciblage », a-t-il expliqué. Poursuivant son intervention, Nérée Noumon a indiqué que des mécanismes de protection sociale étaient déjà en place et avaient commencé à produire des résultats. Il a notamment cité le programme Nafa et le Registre social unifié (RSU), qui constituent, selon lui, des instruments importants pour identifier et accompagner les populations vulnérables. « Le programme Nafa est un programme qui a réussi à cibler les populations vulnérables. Le Registre social unifié est aussi un mécanisme qui n’est pas totalement prêt. Dans le cadre du programme, on va travailler sur la gouvernance. Il y a d’autres partenaires aussi qui sont intéressés par ça, notamment la Banque mondiale, qui contribue à améliorer le RSU. Donc, il y a beaucoup de choses à faire avant que les autorités ne décident de passer à l’action pour réduire les subventions. Et ça se fera toujours en préservant les populations les plus vulnérables et en réduisant, d’une certaine manière, le caractère régressif de ces subventions. » Le représentant résident du FMI a également mis en avant le poids financier des subventions et leur répartition inégale au sein de la population. « Pour vous donner une idée des coûts, plus de 80 % des subventions vont aux 20 % des personnes les plus aisées. Donc, c’est vrai que c’est une chose que personne ne veut avoir dans cette salle, sans compter le poids que ça a sur les budgets. Mais mon message principal ici, c’est qu’il y aura de la communication et des mesures d’accompagnement avant que la décision soit prise. Et on va aussi accompagner les autorités en termes de renforcement des capacités, en se basant sur l’expérience qu’on a eue avec les autres pays. » Abordant ensuite la question de l’endettement supplémentaire, Nérée Noumon a reconnu qu’il s’agissait bien d’une dette supplémentaire, tout en mettant en avant ses conditions financières particulièrement favorables. « Donc, une dette de plus ? Oui, c’est une dette de plus, mais pas n’importe quelle dette. C’est l’une des meilleures dettes qui existent pour les gouvernements, étant donné le taux d’intérêt et les conditions. Donc, déjà, il y a une période de grâce de quatre à cinq ans, il y a des taux d’intérêt très bas. Dans le cadre de cet arrangement, c’est un mix d’un prêt concessionnel pur et d’un prêt un peu moins concessionnel qui vient des ressources générales, mais dont le taux d’intérêt est toujours très, très bas », a-t-il expliqué. Sur la portée de cet accord, le représentant résident du FMI a également évoqué un signe de confiance du conseil d’administration envers les autorités guinéennes, ainsi qu’une reconnaissance de leur engagement à mener les réformes annoncées. « C’est une grande victoire. C’est une grande victoire parce que ça démontre déjà la confiance que le conseil a accordée aux autorités, mais surtout l’engagement des autorités elles-mêmes pour faire les réformes difficiles. L’une des raisons pour lesquelles les programmes du Fonds monétaire sont un peu controversés, c’est que souvent, ce sont des réformes difficiles qu’on recommande. Donc, on recommande, les autorités l’adoptent et donc, dans le cadre des négociations, c’est une grande victoire. Et ça montre vraiment l’engagement des autorités. » Interrogé sur les éventuelles lignes rouges à ne pas franchir dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre du programme, Nérée Noumon a précisé que le suivi reposait essentiellement sur le respect d’un chronogramme de réformes et l’atteinte de repères quantitatifs préalablement définis. « Dans le cadre des programmes du Fonds monétaire, ce qu’on établit, c’est un chronogramme de réformes et de repères quantitatifs à atteindre. Et on fait le suivi, l’évaluation qu’on reporte au conseil d’administration pour la décision du décaissement suivant. Donc, la ligne rouge, au-delà des fondamentaux… Les fondamentaux, c’est vraiment la gouvernance, la transparence, et ça, c’est vraiment quelque chose qui est déjà acquis. Au-delà de cela, il n’y a pas de ligne rouge, à part respecter le chronogramme des réformes. » Pour conclure, le représentant résident du FMI a précisé qu’un éventuel retard dans l’exécution des réformes ne signifiait pas systématiquement une remise en cause du programme. Les autorités peuvent, selon lui, justifier les retards auprès du conseil d’administration et solliciter une dérogation. « Donc, si le chronogramme des réformes n’est pas respecté, les autorités doivent pouvoir justifier le contexte dans lequel il n’a pas été respecté et on soumettra au conseil d’administration les explications. Les autorités pourront bénéficier d’une dérogation. Donc, ne pas respecter un repère structurel, une réforme importante pour les objectifs du programme, n’est pas forcément une fin en soi tant que les justificatifs sont là. » Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article Programme avec le FMI : Nérée Noumon juge la dette guinéenne « parmi les meilleures » et assure qu’aucune mesure n’a été imposée est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: The Multimedia Group CEO Kwasi Twum honoured at UPSA FAF Eminent Achievement Awards
items.description: Founder of the Multimedia Group, Kwasi Twum, has been honoured at the 2026 edition of the Faculty of Accounting and Finance (FAF) Eminent Achievement Awards at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA). The recognition in the Media Enterprise, Corporate Governance and Economic Discourse category on Friday, November 27, celebrates his contribution to Ghana’s media industry. The award particularly commends his role in building Joy FM and its sister platforms into one of the country’s influential radio stations and establishing The Multimedia Group as the leading player in broadcasting and digital media. In announcing the recognition, organisers highlighted Mr Twum’s journey from establishing Joy FM in 1995 to building a multimedia organisation that has contributed to national discourse and created opportunities for generations of media professionals. His legacy, they noted, extends beyond radio, television and digital platforms to include institution-building, public accountability and the strengthening of democratic participation. The 2026 awards are being held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence. Honouring Legacies. Inspiring National Transformation.” The FAF Eminent Achievement Awards were instituted by the Faculty of Accounting and Finance at UPSA to recognise individuals whose professional careers have contributed to excellence, innovation and transformation in accounting, finance, banking and economics. Other awardees were Dhananjay Tripathi – founder of Pharmanova Limited, Dr. Samuel Amo Tobbin – Founder of Tobinco Group of Companies, Joe Jackson – CEO of Dalex Finance, Dr Philip Oti-Mensah – MD and CEO of Universal Merchant Bank (UMB), Chief Dr Doli-Wura Awushi Abdul-Malik Seidu Zakaria – MD of National Investment Bank and Ernest De-Graft Egyir – CEO of Ghana CEO Summit & Chief Executive Networks Ghana. The maiden edition was held in November 2025 under the theme, “Recognising Trailblazers: Driving Excellence and Transformation in Accounting, Finance and Economics.” The award scheme seeks to celebrate leaders whose work has strengthened institutions, advanced professional practice and inspired younger generations. It also forms part of the Faculty’s efforts to bridge the gap between academia and industry through recognition, dialogue, mentorship and collaboration.

Burkina Faso : Après quatre ans d’arrêt, la mine de zinc de Perkoa s’apprête à reprendre ses activités
items.description: Le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, est attendu ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026 à Réo pour présider la cérémonie officielle de relance de la mine de Perkoa. La reprise, confiée à une filiale de la SOPAMIB, mobilise un investissement de 37 milliards de FCFA et prévoit la création de 1 250 emplois directs et indirects. La mine de zinc de Perkoa, située dans la province du Sanguié, s'apprête à reprendre du service après quatre années d'interruption. Ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026, une forte mobilisation des populations a été constatée à Réo, où le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, est attendu pour présider la cérémonie officielle de relance de l'exploitation. Aux abords de la mairie, une foule nombreuse s'est rassemblée pour accueillir le chef de l'État. Des enfants, disposés le long de la route, ont également formé une haie d'honneur à son passage. Sur le site minier, travailleurs, populations et personnalités se sont mobilisés dans une ambiance festive, ponctuée de prestations de troupes traditionnelles. Cette cérémonie marque une nouvelle étape pour l'exploitation minière de Perkoa, dont les activités avaient été suspendues à la suite d'un grave accident survenu en avril 2022. Un drame minier qui avait coûté la vie à huit travailleurs Le 16 avril 2022, une importante inondation des galeries souterraines avait piégé huit travailleurs à l'intérieur de la mine. Malgré les opérations de recherche et de sauvetage, les huit personnes, dont six Burkinabè, un Zambien et un Tanzanien, avaient perdu la vie. Cette tragédie avait entraîné l'arrêt de l'exploitation et profondément marqué les familles des victimes ainsi que le secteur minier burkinabè. Quatre ans plus tard, les autorités engagent la relance du site à travers la SOPAMIB Perkouan SA, une filiale de la Société de participation minière du Burkina (SOPAMIB). 37 milliards de FCFA pour relancer l'exploitation Le projet de reprise repose sur un investissement annoncé de 37 milliards de FCFA. Les prévisions tablent sur une production de 576 000 tonnes de concentré polymétallique sur une période de quatre ans, pour un chiffre d'affaires estimé à 270 milliards de FCFA. Sur le plan socio-économique, la relance devrait permettre la création de 400 emplois directs et d'environ 850 emplois indirects, soit un potentiel de 1 250 emplois au total. Au-delà des perspectives de production et de recettes, la reprise de Perkoa représente un enjeu pour l’emploi local et la redynamisation de l'activité économique dans la province du Sanguié. Après quatre années d'arrêt marquées par le souvenir du drame de 2022, la mine s'apprête ainsi à ouvrir un nouveau chapitre de son histoire. Les conditions de sécurité des travailleurs constitueront un enjeu majeur de cette nouvelle phase d'exploitation. items.title: December 4 declared public holiday for Farmers’ Day
items.description: The government has formally designated Friday, December 4, 2026, as a statutory public holiday to commemorate this year’s National Farmers’ Day celebration. The Ministry of the Interior, in a public announcement, confirmed that the day would be observed as a holiday throughout the country. The annual celebration recognises the contributions of farmers and fishers to Ghana’s agricultural production, food supply and economic growth. Observed on the first Friday of December each year, Farmers’ Day also provides an opportunity to acknowledge the efforts of people engaged in agriculture and draw attention to the importance of the sector to national development. Beyond honouring outstanding farmers and fishers, the occasion offers an opportunity to assess developments in agriculture, examine challenges confronting the sector and renew discussions on policies to strengthen food production, improve food security and enhance the livelihoods of farming communities. The December 4 holiday will therefore allow workers and the general public across the country to join in observing the national occasion. items.title: Rebelión científica tras el anuncio de un colaborador de OpenAI que asegura haber resuelto el gran problema de la física
items.description: La historia se repite, pero esta vez no cuela, según algunos de los mayores expertos en una de las materias más complicadas —y trascendentales— que existen. El joven físico teórico Venkatesa Chandrasekaran acaba de publicar una posible descripción de la gravedad cuántica, uno de los mayores problemas de la física actual, que lleva más de un siglo sin poder resolverse. En su propuesta, aún no revisada por expertos independientes, le da las gracias tanto a OpenAI como a Sam Altman, el director ejecutivo de la compañía. Las formas y el fondo del anuncio son una muestra más del poder de los gigantes de la inteligencia artificial, no solo para atacar problemas que se pensaban irresolubles por mentes humanas, sino para hacerse publicidad con ellos, aunque eso suponga ignorar prácticas básicas del método científico, como la declaración de conflictos de interés. items.title: Burkina Faso : Ancien ravitailleur de groupes terroristes, Issa regrette sa collaboration et appelle à dénoncer les complices
items.description: Illustration Dans la commune de Dî, dans le Sourou, un ancien boutiquier et piroguier de 33 ans reconnaît avoir ravitaillé des hommes ayant rejoint les groupes armés terroristes et facilité leurs déplacements sur le fleuve. Interpellé par les Forces combattantes, il appelle désormais les populations à rompre tout lien avec les personnes impliquées dans le terrorisme. Un témoignage qui illustre les conséquences de la collaboration avec les groupes armés terroristes. À Dî, dans la province du Sourou, Issa, 33 ans, reconnaît avoir entretenu des relations avec des hommes qu'il connaissait depuis l'enfance et qui ont ensuite rejoint les rangs des groupes terroristes. Boutiquier et piroguier de profession, il admet avoir continué à leur fournir des vivres et divers produits, malgré leur implication dans des activités criminelles. Il leur prêtait également ses pirogues pour faciliter leurs traversées du fleuve. Selon son témoignage rapporté par l'Agence d'information du Burkina (AIB), ces anciens amis étaient même devenus ses principaux clients. Une proximité qu'il n'a jamais remise en question, jusqu'au jour où ces hommes ont contribué au déplacement forcé des habitants de son propre village. Des remords après le déplacement de son village Aujourd'hui interpellé par les Forces combattantes, Issa reconnaît avoir commis une faute en maintenant ses relations avec ces individus et en ne signalant pas leurs activités aux autorités compétentes. « C'est cela ma faute. Je ne me suis jamais mis dans la tête un seul jour qu'il fallait les dénoncer aux forces de sécurité », reconnaît-il. Son témoignage révèle également l'existence d'autres formes de soutien logistique aux groupes armés dans la région. Il affirme avoir connu des personnes impliquées dans la vente de bétail, le transport et la livraison de marchandises au profit de ces groupes, sans pour autant les dénoncer. Une attitude qu'il dit aujourd'hui regretter, après avoir lui-même subi les conséquences de l'insécurité et de la collaboration qu'il entretenait avec ces hommes. « Il faut couper les liens » avec les complices Désormais, Issa lance un appel aux populations afin qu'elles ne protègent plus les personnes qui rejoignent les groupes terroristes ou leur apportent une quelconque assistance. « Il faut qu'on coupe les liens avec nos amis, connaissances ou proches qui choisissent d'intégrer les rangs des terroristes ou de les aider. Il y a plusieurs canaux pour les dénoncer et si on ne le fait pas, c'est une complicité qui finira par nous coûter cher, comme c'est le cas aujourd'hui avec moi », prévient-il. 199 : Centre national d'appels, gratuit et disponible 24 heures sur 24. 71 20 33 33 et 68 24 44 44 : alertes par WhatsApp. 17 : Police nationale. 16 : Gendarmerie nationale. 1010 : Centre national de veille et d'alerte. Par ailleurs, le président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a régulièrement appelé les personnes ayant rejoint les groupes armés à déposer les armes. L’article Burkina Faso : Ancien ravitailleur de groupes terroristes, Issa regrette sa collaboration et appelle à dénoncer les complices est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Régionales en Guinée : matériel, sécurité, contentieux… la DGE rassure pour les 375 circonscriptions
items.description: À deux jours des élections régionales prévues le 29 novembre 2026, la Direction générale des élections (DGE) fait le point sur l’état des préparatifs. Acheminement du matériel électoral, formation des superviseurs et des membres des bureaux de vote, gestion du contentieux, dispositif sécuritaire : l’institution affirme avoir pris les dispositions nécessaires pour permettre la tenue du scrutin dans les meilleures conditions. Lors d’un point de presse animé ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026, le directeur général des élections, Mohamed Aly Condé, a d’abord insisté sur le travail collectif effectué au sein de son institution. « Je profite de cette occasion pour remercier l’ensemble des collaborateurs qui sont ici présents aujourd’hui, à commencer par monsieur le directeur général adjoint, l’ensemble des directeurs et chefs de service. Parce qu’on a l’habitude de dire que c’est une équipe qui gagne. Donc, si tout est fait aujourd’hui à la Direction générale des élections, ce n’est pas le directeur général seul qui le rend, mais en grande partie l’équipe qui m’accompagne à tout moment. Et c’est ce qui fait qu’on est arrivé là où nous sommes aujourd’hui. » Selon le responsable de la DGE, les commissions chargées de recevoir et de traiter les candidatures ont notamment été installées dans les différentes communes, avec une commission spéciale pour Conakry et une commission nationale de validation. Sur le plan logistique, le DGE assure que le matériel électoral sensible a été acheminé dans l’ensemble des circonscriptions. « Sur les 375 circonscriptions, nous avons aujourd’hui acheminé le matériel sensible à tous les niveaux. J’ai des techniciens actuellement qui peuvent vous donner beaucoup plus de détails, mais au stade où nous sommes, on peut dire que les kits, les urnes, les bulletins, les fournitures sont aujourd’hui présents dans toutes les circonscriptions, en tout cas dans les 375. » La DGE a également procédé au déploiement de superviseurs chargés de suivre le déroulement du scrutin sur le terrain. « À chaque scrutin sur le terrain, la DGE recrute ou contracte des personnes qui sont des superviseurs et des préparateurs ou des agents de sécurité. Ce sont pour nous-mêmes nos représentants qu’on envoie sur le terrain et qui font en sorte que tout ce qui se passe sur le terrain, depuis l’ouverture de la journée de vote jusqu’à la fin de la machine et jusqu’à la transmission des procès-verbaux et des pièces annexées, se passe de manière régulière et qu’ils soient les yeux et les oreilles de la Direction générale des élections qui nous remontent ces informations. » Au total, 46 superviseurs ont été déployés à travers le pays, selon le directeur général des élections. Autre volet du dispositif : la formation des membres des bureaux de vote. Mohamed Aly Condé affirme que cette opération se déroule dans les différentes directions régionales. « La formation des membres des bureaux de vote se passe très bien aujourd’hui sur l’ensemble des directions régionales. » La DGE a également organisé des sessions de préparation consacrées au contentieux électoral, notamment avec des magistrats et des acteurs du barreau. « Une élection, ce n’est pas seulement l’organisation matérielle. Le processus, ce n’est pas seulement de recevoir des candidatures, de publier des listes de candidatures, d’établir les listes électorales ou bien de proclamer simplement les résultats. Il y a une autre étape encore très importante qui est la gestion du contentieux électoral. » Le directeur général des élections explique que la DGE a récemment réuni à Kindia des magistrats ainsi que des acteurs du barreau afin de renforcer la préparation du dispositif juridictionnel. « Nous avons réuni récemment à Kindia l’ensemble des magistrats et même du barreau de Conakry et de l’intérieur pour les soutenir dans ce sens. Cela a été fait. » Contrairement aux élections présidentielle, législatives ou communales, les élections régionales ne mobiliseront pas l’ensemble de la population. Le scrutin est indirect : seuls les conseillers communaux sont appelés à voter pour élire les conseillers régionaux. Mohamed Aly Condé insiste sur cette particularité, qui explique notamment le faible niveau de mobilisation observé dans l’espace public. « Les élections vont se tenir simplement dans les communes puisque ça concerne les conseillers communaux. C’est eux seulement qui vont avoir la chance d’exprimer leur vote en faveur d’autres conseillers communaux qui ont été candidats pour être au niveau du conseil régional. » Il précise : « C’est un scrutin indirect qui fait que c’est simplement les conseillers communaux dans les différentes communes qui vont voter encore une fois pour d’autres parmi eux qui ont bien voulu être au conseil régional. C’est un suffrage indirect. Ça va se passer à la majorité à un tour. Ça veut dire que celui qui aura la majorité parmi les candidats est d’office élu conseiller régional. Vous n’avez pas ce tapage comme si c’était les législatives et la présidentielle. Parce que, encore une fois, même ceux qui seront candidats, ils n’auront pas à faire campagne auprès de leurs homologues conseillers communaux dans les communes. Ça ne sort pas de ce périmètre en fait. » Mohamed Aly Condé estime que, dans certaines communes, les opérations pourraient être bouclées en quelques heures. « Je prends l’exemple d’un district qui n’a pas 45 conseillers. Alors, on ouvre le bureau de vote à 8h, vous verrez que, au plus tard à 10h, le vote est terminé. Ça, c’est au plus tard. Il y a des communes qui ont 11 conseillers et dans d’autres 15, le vote de 15 personnes ou de 10 personnes va prendre combien de temps ? Donc, ce qui fait que ce n’est pas ce même effet que les élections générales présidentielles et législatives. » La DGE a également mis en place une commission de veille juridique. Celle-ci doit suivre les éventuelles violations des droits des candidats et contribuer à leur rétablissement lorsqu’une irrégularité est signalée. « Les élections sont éminemment juridiques. Pour ceux qui savent, je ne dis pas qu’il n’y a pas d’autres aspects, il y a beaucoup d’aspects techniques, il y a beaucoup d’aspects financiers. Mais en fait, une élection, c’est d’abord le cadre juridique. C’est une Constitution qui fixe les règles du jeu, c’est le Code électoral qui définit comment est-ce qu’il faut organiser et tout ça. » Il précise le rôle de cette commission : « À notre niveau ici, à chaque fois qu’il y a une élection, nous mettons en place cette commission de veille juridique pour faire en sorte que le corps électoral, aucun candidat ne soit privé de ses droits. Il faut informer de la violation d’une situation, faire en sorte que cette situation soit rétablie et que le candidat soit rétabli dans ses droits. Une fois que ce tribunal ou cette cour est saisie par ces candidats, on notifie à la DGE qu’un tel candidat a exercé un recours contre vos résultats. C’est à ce moment-là que cette commission de veille juridique aussi se met en place pour pouvoir travailler, préparer la défense de la Direction générale des élections. » Au volet électoral s’ajoute enfin la question sécuritaire. La DGE indique travailler avec le gouvernement pour sécuriser les bureaux et centres de vote. « Il y a aussi l’aspect sécuritaire qu’on est en train de préparer parce qu’effectivement, on a un contact avec le gouvernement. Ils sont aussi des acteurs de premier plan dans le processus électoral. Ils vont permettre ce dimanche de sécuriser partout où nous allons mettre les isoloirs et les bureaux de vote. » Au terme de son intervention, Mohamed Aly Condé assure que la DGE se considère prête pour le scrutin du 29 novembre. « Je pense très bien que nous sommes à jour. On est à deux jours de l’avant-veille, demain samedi, le dimanche matin, on est prêts que le scrutin puisse se passer dans les conditions les meilleures. » Mayi Cissé L’article Régionales en Guinée : matériel, sécurité, contentieux… la DGE rassure pour les 375 circonscriptions est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: EOCO announces fact-finding mission with INTERPOL to QNET’s head office in Malaysia to combat ‘Model Q’ scams and human trafficking
items.description: The Economic and Organised Crime Office in Ghana, has proactively conducted a fact-finding mission to the head office of QNET in Malaysia. QNET officials in Malaysia received the mission. QNET, an international lifestyle and wellness e-commerce and direct-selling leader, is taking firm steps to correct widespread misconceptions and combat the criminal misuse of its corporate name. The company is clarifying the stark distinction between its legitimate global business operations and the predatory “Model Q” criminal networks that falsely claim association with the brand to exploit vulnerable job seekers. The narrative surrounding QNET has frequently been manipulated by malicious actors who use the company’s reputation as a shield for their illicit activities, particularly in human trafficking and financial fraud schemes. QNET has consistently and forcefully condemned these criminal misuse tactics, emphasising that its business model is strictly regulated and compliant with international standards. To address these misrepresentations, QNET has been working closely with authorities to provide accurate information about its operations. As detailed in a recent official press release from the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), the company’s engagement with law enforcement has been pivotal in exposing these criminal strategies: “Delegates received briefings from QNET’s team to examine how direct-selling structures and brands are being exploited by criminal syndicates. The delegation was also presented with cases of brand impersonation involving fake scholarships and fraudulent employment offers falsely linked to Quest International University (QIU).” These briefings serve to debunk the fraudulent narratives that criminal networks use to lure victims. QNET does not engage in, condone, or profit from these criminal networks’ activities. On the contrary, these syndicates are parasitic, relying on brand impersonation to deceive individuals into falling for human trafficking and smuggling traps. QNET’s commitment to truth extends to public education. QNET has reaffirmed its commitment to public education, compliance, and anti-fraud cooperation with its anti-scam campaign christened ‘QNET Against Scams”. The company encourages the public to verify all recruitment and employment opportunities through official QNET channels and to be highly cautious of any entity requesting payment for guaranteed jobs or promising unrealistic earnings, as these are hallmark signs of the fraud schemes that QNET is actively fighting. By shedding light on the mechanics of these scams, QNET is reclaiming its identity and ensuring that the public understands the legitimate nature of its direct-selling business.

items.title: Enfants autistes : des mères face à l’oubli (Par Matel BOCOUM)
items.description: À l’heure des 16 jours d’activisme contre les violences faites aux femmes et aux filles, des voix attirent l’attention sur les enfants à besoins spécifiques et leurs mamans, qui livrent chaque jour de multiples batailles. Le quotidien est éprouvant pour celles accusées d’avoir donné naissance à des « enfants de djinns » ou à des « enfants de la honte », en raison de comportements atypiques que leur entourage peine à comprendre. Dans certaines communautés traditionalistes, des manifestations liées à l’autisme, comme l’hypersensibilité aux bruits ou les crises d’agitation, sont parfois interprétées comme des signes de possession ou de présence d’un esprit surnaturel. Ces croyances renforcent l’isolement et la stigmatisation. Ailleurs, le tableau n’est pas moins sombre. Le retrait ou le désengagement du conjoint plongent souvent les mères dans une détresse psychologique et des choix difficiles à faire. « Mon mari n’a jamais voulu accepter notre fille, qui a aujourd’hui 10 ans. Il estime que, dans sa famille, il n’y a pas ce genre d’enfants. » Ce témoignage d’une jeune dame est loin d’être singulier. Nombreuses sont les mères d’enfants présentant un Trouble du spectre de l’autisme (Tsa) qui sont privées de soutien familial, psychologique et financier. Dans nos sociétés africaines, elles affrontent souvent seules les jugements et le rejet. Leur quotidien est fait d’incertitudes et de sacrifices. Elles doivent trouver des solutions pour soigner leurs enfants, leur assurer une éducation, leur socialisation et préserver leur équilibre familial. Obtenir un diagnostic, accéder aux soins, financer les prises en charge et trouver une école adaptée relèvent parfois du parcours du combattant. Faute d’accompagnement, les familles de ces enfants à besoins spécifiques font face à des dépenses souvent exorbitantes. Pour certaines mamans, le combat va jusqu’au sacrifice de leur vie professionnelle. Beaucoup ont dû démissionner, renoncer à leur emploi ou mettre entre parenthèses leurs ambitions pour se consacrer à leurs enfants. Une décision qui les prive d’autonomie financière et les fragilise davantage, dans un contexte marqué par l’absence de dispositifs d’accompagnement adaptés. Alors que, dans d’autres sociétés, les troubles du neurodéveloppement sont davantage reconnus et accompagnés, les différences continuent trop souvent de susciter incompréhension, rejet et honte dans plusieurs pays africains comme le nôtre conduisant à la marginalisation des enfants et de leurs familles. Pourtant, certains enfants autistes développent des aptitudes remarquables, parfois associées au syndrome du savant. Ils présentent des capacités intellectuelles supérieures à la moyenne dans des domaines précis. Chez d’autres, leurs difficultés de communication peuvent aussi masquer leurs capacités. Une publication intitulée « Syndrome du savant : caractéristiques cliniques et troubles neurodéveloppementaux associés » indique que ce syndrome concernerait environ une personne sur dix parmi celles présentant un trouble du spectre de l’autisme (Tsa), avec une prédominance masculine estimée à quatre hommes pour une femme. « Ce syndrome se caractérise par des capacités cognitives extraordinaires dans des domaines spécifiques, tels que la mémoire, le calcul ou les compétences artistiques, malgré d’importantes déficiences neurodéveloppementales », renseigne la publication. Tous les enfants présentant un Trouble du spectre de l’autisme (Tsa) ne possèdent pas de tels dons. Mais la reconnaissance de leurs capacités reste un enjeu. Leur potentiel n’est pas toujours exploré et leurs particularités, comprises. Pourtant, chaque enfant, quelles que soient ses différences, possède une dignité et des droits. Il mérite d’être reconnu, accompagné et intégré. Les 16 jours d’activisme mettent en lumière les injustices et les déséquilibres qui fragilisent les femmes. Au-delà de cette campagne, il est essentiel de porter un regard plus humain sur ces mères et leurs enfants. Accompagner un enfant autiste et lutter contre son exclusion, c’est aussi protéger sa mère, reconnaître sa souffrance et soutenir ses efforts. Ce combat ne devrait pas être le sien seul, mais celui de toute la société. matel.bocoum@lesoleil.sn

items.title: Stonebwoy releases ‘Marry You’ ahead of ‘TORCHER III’ album
items.description: Ghanaian musician Stonebwoy has released his latest single, “Marry You”, the first official offering from his forthcoming album, TORCHER III: Flames of Love . Produced by US-based Ghanaian producer Selasi, “Marry You” sees the multi-award-winning artiste further explore the romantic sensibilities that have long been a defining element of his musical repertoire. Rooted in his signature Afro-Dancehall sound, the record pairs rich melodies with heartfelt lyricism, capturing the excitement of finding love and the deeper emotional commitment that comes with choosing a partner. At the heart of the track, Stonebwoy delivers an affectionate declaration of love, expressing his desire to build a lifelong union with his partner. Beyond its inviting melody, memorable hook and chorus, the record explores the deeper foundations of lasting relationships, emphasising faith, devotion and the strength of a bond capable of withstanding external pressures. “Marry You” arrives with a music video that shows a deeply personal side of Stonebwoy’s family. Shot in Atlanta and directed by Kwaku Kwakye, the visuals open with Stonebwoy and his wife, Dr Louisa, exchanging vows before transitioning into a series of intimate family moments featuring their two children. In a special reveal, the couple also announce that they are expecting another addition to their family, with Dr Louisa revealing her baby bump. “Marry You” offers a glimpse into the creative direction of TORCHER III , the third instalment of THE TORCHER series. Anchored in the concept Flames of Love (FOL), the forthcoming project marks a thematic evolution that places greater emphasis on love-oriented narratives while exploring the complexities of romance, relationships, passion, affection and emotional connection. The Flames of Love concept reimagines the fiery identity associated with THE TORCHER series, giving it a new thematic expression rooted in the intensity, warmth and emotional power of love. Rather than departing from the energy that has defined THE TORCHER and TORCHER II , Stonebwoy channels that same passion into stories of romance, desire, devotion and lasting companionship, positioning TORCHER III to reveal a more intimate and emotionally expressive dimension of his artistry. La CAF introduit la VAR dès la phase de groupes des compétitions interclubs 2026/27
items.description: La Confédération Africaine de Football (CAF) introduira l’assistance vidéo à l’arbitrage (VAR) lors de l’ensemble des rencontres de la phase de groupes de la TotalEnergies CAF Ligue des Champions 2026/27 et de la TotalEnergies CAF Coupe de la Confédération 2026/27. Il s’agira d’une première dans l’histoire des compétitions interclubs de la CAF, puisque la VAR était jusqu’à présent uniquement utilisée à partir des phases à élimination directe de ces deux compétitions, indique l'instance continentale dans un communiqué. Alors que la phase de groupes de la TotalEnergies CAF Coupe de la Confédération débute ce vendredi 27 novembre 2026, l’introduction de cette technologie permettra d’apporter un soutien supplémentaire aux arbitres et contribuera significativement au renforcement des standards de l’arbitrage africain, avec l’ambition de les hisser parmi les meilleurs au monde, relève la même source. Sous la direction du Président de la CAF, Patrice Motsepe, l’instance dirigeante du football africain a fait du développement des infrastructures, de l’investissement dans les nouvelles technologies, du renforcement des capacités des arbitres et de la professionnalisation de ses compétitions, des axes prioritaires de son action, souligne le communiqué. Et d'ajouter que cette mise en œuvre a été rendue possible grâce au programme de l’Académie VAR de la CAF, qui a permis de déployer les équipements technologiques nécessaires et de former des arbitres vidéo qualifiés (VMO) dans les six unions zonales de la CAF. Des formations dédiées à la VAR, organisées à l’échelle des Unions Zonales et du continent, contribuent à élargir le vivier d’arbitres vidéo compétents et expérimentés, précise la même source, relevant que cette montée en compétences des officiels permettra de renforcer la cohérence des décisions arbitrales, de consolider la confiance dans l’arbitrage africain et de contribuer au développement du football sur le continent. La CAF poursuit ainsi le déploiement progressif de la VAR dans ses principales compétitions, notamment la TotalEnergies CAF Coupe d’Afrique des Nations, la TotalEnergies CAF Coupe d’Afrique des Nations Féminine ainsi que les compétitions interclubs de la CAF, conclut la même source. The post La CAF introduit la VAR dès la phase de groupes des compétitions interclubs 2026/27 appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Ogun 2027: Court dismisses Hunye’s suits against Adeola’s APC candidacy
items.description: …Adeola hails judgment …as Hunye heads to Court of Appeal By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Federal High Court sitting in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday dismissed two suits filed by Hon. Abayomi Semako Hunye challenging the emergence of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Delivering judgment in the two consolidated suits, Justice Okeke held that the cases lacked merit and consequently dismissed them. The suits, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1127/2026 and FHC/AB/126/2026, were instituted by Hunye against the APC, Senator Adeola and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), challenging the process through which Adeola emerged as the party’s governorship candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Adeola commended the judiciary, describing the decision as a vindication of the rule of law and the judicial process. In a statement issued by his media adviser, Chief Kayode Odunaro, the senator expressed satisfaction with the outcome while appreciating his legal team for what he described as their painstaking efforts in defending the suits. Adeola said, “I want to commend the Honourable Justice for his erudite judgment in these cases challenging my overwhelming and widely accepted victory in our party primary. I also commend my legal team for the painstaking defense put up during the process. “This victory is yet another milestone in our quest for equity and justice in the Ogun State 2027 election. To God be the glory once again.” The senator said that despite the legal challenges, he had remained focused on consolidating support for his candidacy across the state through engagements with political stakeholders and other interest groups. He added that his engagements had also included the presentation of his nine-pillar ITESIWAJU Agenda, which he described as his development blueprint for Ogun State. According to him, the court’s decision would allow him to concentrate more fully on preparations for the 2027 governorship election and take his campaign message to voters across the state. Adeola also urged APC members and his supporters, irrespective of their political affiliations, to remain united and focused, stressing that his ambition was driven by a desire to serve the people and contribute to the development of Ogun State. However, Hunye has rejected the outcome of the proceedings and indicated his intention to appeal the judgment. In a statement titled, “Our Legal Journey Continues to the Court of Appeal,” Hunye described the Federal High Court as the first stage of the judicial process, insisting that the appellate court would provide another opportunity for his legal team to pursue the issues raised in the suits. He reaffirmed his commitment to constitutional due process, internal party democracy, and the rule of law, saying his decision to continue with the litigation was informed by the need to ensure fairness and strict compliance with established legal and electoral procedures. “The Federal High Court is just the first court of hearing, while the Court of Appeal is the next port of call,” Hunye stated. He expressed confidence in the appellate process, adding that his legal team was prepared to present its arguments before the Court of Appeal. “Where questions of fairness, legality, and electoral compliance remain unresolved, our legal team is fully prepared to test every issue before the Court of Appeal. We have faith in the appellate process and remain confident that, in time, truth and legality will prevail,” he said. Hunye further appealed to his supporters, APC members, and the general public to remain calm, peaceful, and law-abiding as the legal process continues. He maintained that his decision to pursue the matter was not merely about political ambition but also about defending due process, strengthening internal party democracy, and ensuring that political parties adhere to constitutional and electoral requirements. items.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
items.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. The reported immigration charges do not amount to convictions for romance fraud. The post Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Don’t be in a hurry for titles; prioritise hard work and integrity – Nana Appiah Dankawoso II advises youth
items.description: Chairman of the second edition of the FAF Eminent Achievement Awards, Nana Appiah Dankawoso II, has urged young people to prioritise learning, hard work and integrity over the pursuit of titles and wealth. Addressing the ceremony at the Kofi Ohene-Konadu Auditorium of the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), on Friday, November 27, he said young people should focus on building their character and reputations as they work towards achieving success. He said the seven awardees had established successful businesses across banking, media, finance, pharmaceuticals and other sectors, with their contributions reflected in jobs created, families supported, and confidence in Ghanaian businesses strengthened. “But every great tree started as a seed, and every awardee here once sat where our students sit today. To the young people in this hall, I say, do not be in a hurry for titles. Be in a hurry to learn, to work earnestly, and to keep your name clean,” he said. Nana Appiah Dankawoso II cautioned that while wealth could be rebuilt, a damaged reputation was much harder to restore. “Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, in the good book, Proverbs 22, verse 1, talks about good name and riches. And it says, choose good name,” he added. He also congratulated the seven awardees, describing the recognition from an institution that trains future professionals as more than an award, but an opportunity to continue making a difference in society. “The recognition you receive tonight comes from a university that shapes the professionals of tomorrow, and that makes it more than a plaque. It is a chance to keep lifting others as you climb,” he said. He commended UPSA and its Faculty of Accounting and Finance for establishing a tradition of recognising excellence, expressing hope that the initiative would continue to grow.

items.title: CBN targets $1.5bn monthly diaspora dollar inflows
items.description: — Vows to deploy external reserves against FX shocks To unveil regulatory rule book next year By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is targeting $1.5 billion monthly diaspora remittance inflows by the first half of 2027, following the achievement of its $1 billion monthly target, while pledging to deploy external reserves to cushion the economy against external shocks. CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, disclosed this at the 61st Annual Bankers Dinner organised by the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN) in Lagos. Speaking on the foreign exchange market and the country’s external buffers, Cardoso said: “I am pleased that this milestone has actually been achieved, towards increased monthly remittances of $1 billion. Our next target is $1.5 billion by the end of the first half of 2027.” He said Nigeria was considerably better equipped to manage external shocks than it was three years ago, following reforms that strengthened macroeconomic fundamentals and external buffers. “The external buffers we have built provide greater resilience, and the Central Bank of Nigeria stands ready to deploy its reserves when necessary to address disorderly market conditions and mitigate the impact of shocks,” he said. According to him, the CBN’s responsibility was not to target a particular exchange rate level but to safeguard market stability, deepen liquidity and support orderly price discovery. “Recent short-term movements should be viewed in the context of strengthened macroeconomic fundamentals and the outlook for 2027,” he said, adding that volatility was an inherent feature of global financial markets. Cardoso also announced plans to introduce a regulatory rule book next year as part of efforts to strengthen the financial system, improve accountability and ensure that financial institutions operate within a clear and consistent regulatory framework. He said the financial system required governance, transparency, accountability and decision-making grounded in clear analysis and consistent application of regulatory standards. The CBN governor urged banks to strengthen treasury expertise, expand hedging and risk management products, support exporters and provide more effective services to businesses engaged in international trade. He also announced plans to deepen Nigeria’s financial market infrastructure, saying the apex bank would work with market participants to launch interbank repo and overnight interest rate swap markets in the first quarter of 2027. “To further deepen liquidity and improve market efficiency, we will work with market participants to launch the interbank repo and overnight interest swap markets in the first quarter of 2027,” he said. Cardoso said Nigeria’s removal from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) grey list in October 2025 reflected sustained efforts across government, regulatory authorities and the financial sector to strengthen the country’s framework against money laundering, terrorist financing and related financial crimes. The post CBN targets $1.5bn monthly diaspora dollar inflows appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test
items.description: Nollywood actress Adesua Etomi-Wellington has celebrated testing negative for cancer after months of medical procedures, hospital visits and uncertainty over her health. The actress announced the development on Friday in an Instagram video, expressing gratitude to God following the latest result from her medical tests. “The doctor just called me back with the result from the lab, no cancer… God is good,” she said. The video showed some of the medical procedures she underwent, while other pictures revealed bruises on her body and redness beneath one of her eyes. Etomi-Wellington also shared a video of friends and well-wishers celebrating the result with her. Reflecting on her experience, the actress described 2026 as one of the most difficult periods of her life, explaining that her reduced public appearances were linked to her health struggles. “2026 really tried it. I know I’ve been quieter than usual this year (and that’s saying something), but behind the silence were some of the most difficult months of my life,” she wrote. She disclosed that the ordeal involved several medical procedures, scans, injections and hospital visits, adding that she received treatment from medical teams in Nigeria and the United States. “This year threw everything at me, but by the grace of God, I am NOT EASILY BROKEN,” she added. The actress also expressed appreciation to her husband, singer and politician Bankole Wellington, popularly known as Banky W, their children, friends and family members for supporting her throughout the difficult period. “To my friends and family who prayed for me, stood in the gap and held me through some of my darkest days, I will never take your love for granted,” she wrote. The health update comes two days after the couple released a gospel song, On My Way , on November 25 to celebrate their ninth wedding anniversary. The track, credited to Etomi-Wellington, who performs under the musical name Susu, and Banky W, is the lead single from their forthcoming joint album, Not Easily Broken , expected in 2027. The actress described the song as “the soundtrack to our testimony and thanksgiving”, linking its message to their personal experiences. The couple have previously spoken about their health challenges. In May 2024, Banky W disclosed that he had undergone his fourth surgery for cancer after earlier procedures to remove cancerous tumours. Etomi-Wellington also revealed in March 2025 that she battled hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe form of pregnancy sickness, during her second pregnancy. The condition left her ill for months and required hospitalisation before she underwent an emergency Caesarean section. The post Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test appeared first on Vanguard News .
